Definition: {properly, a judgeship, i.e. jurisdiction; by implication, a district (as ruled by a judge); generally, a region}
BiblicalUsage: A province is a district under a ruler, and the Aramaic word is used where empires count their lands: Daniel is made ruler over the whole province of Babylon, Shadrach and his friends are set over the affairs of the province, and the enemies of the Jews warn the king that Jerusalem has made insurrection in times past.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the province is where God puts His people to work: Daniel ruled a pagan province without bowing to it, and the same God who set him over Babylon kept him through the furnace.
